newsitem.title: BURUNDI: Burundi army accused of killing over 150 civilians.
newsitem.headline: Burundi army accused of killing over 150 civilians.

text.p: Foreign aid workers said on Friday troops killed more than 150 civilians in the southern Burundian region of Bururi in reprisals after attacks by Hutu rebels but the army denied the charge.
"Armed bands attacked in the three communes overnight on Monday. They killed 13 people, but the army didn't kill anybody," said army spokesman Lieutenant-Colonel Isaie Nibizi.

The aid workers, who declined to be identified, said troops killed more than 100 people at Mugara in Rumonge commune and 51 people including women and children on the hills near Maramvya in Burambi commune last Monday.
They said more civilians were killed at Mubuga in fighting between the army and rebels. They said the army killings at Mugara and hills near Maramvya followed attacks by Hutu rebels.
Dozens of wounded civilians were being treated on Friday at a hospital in central Bujumbura, about 180 km (110 km) north of the sites of the reported killings.
Burundi's Tutsi-dominated army is involved in a vicious civil war against Hutu rebels and both sides are frequently accused by human rights groups of massacring civilians.
The U.N. Human Rights agency said in January about 1,000 people were killed since last December, most by the army.
More than 150,000 people -- mainly civilians -- have been killed in Burundi since October 1993 when soldiers murdered the country's first elected Hutu president in an attempted coup.
